why: I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one. Item 1: builder step 2 says to add a "### subtract(a, b)" entry ("it is exported but undocumented today") and a "### clamp(x, lo, hi)" entry. Item 2: verifier Check 3 doesn't hard-code the function names. Its script reads them from math.js at the PR head and prints "exports: ...", which would be add, subtract, multiply and clamp. It exits 1 with MISSING if any of them lacks a README heading. The brief also says plainly that subtract "must now be covered too". The FAIL rule is "any exported function has no description in README.md". Item 3: verifier Check 2 uses a.throws(()=>clamp(5,10,0),RangeError) and a second call. Passing the RangeError class to assert.throws makes it an instanceof check, and the FAIL rule covers "throws something that is not a RangeError".
